My understanding of the Battle of Agincourt (this is off the top of my head based on some historical account I read years ago) is that the severely outnumbered English occupied a hilltop (the movie had the English downhill). It did rain the night before (movie had that). The English protected their long bows from the rain while the French allegedly had their crossbow saturated with water further reducing their range even though the longbow far outranged the crossbow anyway. The movie was still worth the watch. I really enjoy medieval movies and they often inspire me to read up on medieval history as it's often very entertaining to note the historical inaccuracies and you often learn about some real bad asses that are sometimes downplayed in cinema. A good example would be Robert the Bruce from Braveheart, in the movie they make him out to be kind of a pussy. In history the guy won more than a couple of one on one duels on the battlefield where knights surveying the field prior to battle would sometimes challenge one another to single combat often to the death.

I have not been able to find any information about the layout of the field other than it was flanked by two small forests which prevented the French cavalry from encircling the archers and the fact that it was covered in mud from weeks of rainfall. The mud played a significant role in the English victory. While the knights themselves were heavily armored, the horses only had minimal protection surrounding the head. The mud slowed the charge down enough that the archers could get shots in at the legs bringing the horses down. One thing I was surprised to find was that Henry himself joined in the melee and took an axe blow to the head. Its so fascinating to see leaders back then actually joining the fights themselves, something you don't see that often after the early modern era. You can see how that strategy can go badly when Gustavus Adolphus died in the initial charge in the Battle of Lutzen which effectively ended Sweden's participation in the Thirty Years War.
